pr_title: don't set NodeNetworkUnavailable condition on the cloud-provider node controller
pr_body:
The route controller allready handles the NodeNetworkUnavailable condition, there is no need for the specific GCE check on the node controller.


https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a51b8ce45693c61875751690b40ce528f3c77b0c/pkg/controller/route/route_controller.go#L263-L273

This is also seems to depend on the route_controller and the cloud_allocator to remove the condition, if none of those are running nodes will be tainted forever

/kind bug
/kind cleanup
```release-note
NONE
```

Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118934

issue_context.title: Do not set NetworkUnavailable condition on node controller for GCE
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

This pertains more for clusters running in GCP but not necessarily in a GKE environment. Clusters that using a CNI supporting overlay such as Calico, do not need explicit routes to be created on the infrastructure level, meaning that the route controller should not be necessary. 

The following snippet https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/node/node_controller.go#L456-L468 sets the `NetworkUnavailable` condition for new GCE nodes when a new node is picked up by the node controller. This condition is supposed to be removed later by the route controller in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/52457842d155743f0e3fc57ade87251cca37d375/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/route/route_controller.go#L397. However, as stated above there are cases where the route controller is not needed and should not be running.

When Calico is deployed in such a way that the calico-node pods are ignoring any and all `NoSchedule` taints including the cloudprovider's `node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized` taint (which we consider reasonable for a system pod such as calico), the above check creates the following race condition:  a Calico pod may start and set the node network conditions (`NetworkUnavailable` to false) before the node controller reconciles the node. After that the node controller picks up the node and sets the `NetworkUnavailable` condition to an otherwise healthy node.

Leaving aside the race condition itself, I have to ask whether the check is meaningful in the first place. AFAIK, the kubelet in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/52457842d155743f0e3fc57ade87251cca37d375/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L338 ~~already sets the same condition, so I am not sure if there is any particular reason for the node controller to make the same operation.~~ Kubelet only sets the condition for `gce` provider, but clusters should already be using kubelet with cloudprovider=`external`


### What did you expect to happen?

For the node controller to not set the `NetworkUnavailable` condition unnecessarily. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

An easy way to do it with a custom CCM image is to introduce some delay in the node sync loop, enough for pods such as calico-node to start on that node.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

review_comments: also this looks wrong, since the cluster can be created with ip aliases, and not routes

Not sure if this is still safe to remove, I think this was added due to a similar check we have in kubelet to add this condition before initialization. It's possible this check is no longer needed though but I'm misisng context on it. @jprzychodzen might know.

> at this point the node is tainted, see line 427

Not sure I follow, but the condition is here _because_ node controller is about to remove the taint, allowing workloads to schedule on this node. The condition here ensures pods won't schedule without route controller doing a second pass on the node.

> and the route controller will set the corresponding condition if necessary 

Even with route controller applying the condition, there is still a window of time between when nodes are schedulable and the condition is applied. Note that route controller does not watch Nodes and instead does a full sync of all nodes every 5 minutes by default. So in the worse case scenario you'll have a 5 minute window of pods being scheduled without networking. This is also why kubelet applied the condition as well, to ensure pods are not scheduable until Node is synced by route controller at least once.

but this is already added in the kubelet, no?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/52457842d155743f0e3fc57ade87251cca37d375/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L336-L345

why do we need to add it twice?

I think the https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/52457842d155743f0e3fc57ade87251cca37d375/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L337 may cause some issues after all.

Based on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/52457842d155743f0e3fc57ade87251cca37d375/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_network.go#L30-L40

The `kubelet.cloud` should be nil - using the `external` cloudprovider which should be the generic case now - and therefor the condition is not set. However @andrewsykim I must ask and please correct me, but wouldn't such a scenario that you describe be applicable to any cloudprovider/setup that rely on the route controller and is not named `gce` ? And if so, shouldn't we strive for a common solution instead of relying on special/legacy "gceism"s as the PR title eloquently put ? 

From the previous point, maybe kubelet should always set the condition then. For overlay networks Calico/Cilium are already managing the condition and for other cases that include the route controller, we know that it is already updating the condition. I am not familiar enough to comment about the practices of other overlay-supporting CNIs though. 

Maybe a kubelet configuration flag as the comments should be the way forward such that it controls whether the kubelet is setting the condition on node creation is more flexible.

to close on this, Dan perfectly summarizes it here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120486#issuecomment-1710410069 , the network plugin on the nodes, if it depends on the PodCIDR fields to be populated, should not mark the node as ready.
In GCE this is already done by netd https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/netd/blob/df4eab3811e20430b21ec8ec9113b407c93a6cb7/scripts/install-cni.sh#L131 , so this taint is redundant, as the node will not be ready until the cni config file is present
